label: alg:gs-reduce-to-hecke-nf
title: Gröbner–Shirshov reduction to Hecke normal form
html:
Algorithm (Gröbner–Shirshov reduction to Hecke normal form). Quotient a braid-word w \in B_n by the Hecke relation \sigma_i^2 = (q - q^{-1})\sigma_i + 1 to produce its canonical representative \mathrm{NF}(w) \in H_n(q).

Input

  • Braid word w \in B_n (output of Step 1 / alg:categorical-action).
  • Substrate parameter q \in R (symbolic or pinned to q_0).

Output

  • Hecke normal form \mathrm{NF}(w) = \sum_{i} c_i(q)\, T_{w_i} as an R-linear combination of basis elements T_{w_i} indexed by permutations w_i \in S_n (the standard H_n(q) basis), with coefficients c_i(q) \in R[q, q^{-1}].

Algorithm

1. Initialize NF ← w (read as a formal product of σ_i^{±1}).
2. Repeat until no rewrite rule applies:
   a. Apply braid relations σ_iσ_jσ_i = σ_jσ_iσ_j (|i-j| = 1)
      to canonicalise commuting / braided pairs.
   b. Apply the Hecke relation σ_i² = (q - q^{-1})σ_i + 1
      to eliminate self-squares, generating two summands.
   c. For σ_i^{-1}: rewrite σ_i^{-1} = σ_i − (q − q^{-1}) using
      the same Hecke quotient.
3. Collect like terms; output as Σ c_i(q) · T_{w_i}.

Correctness conditions

Correctness rests on two upstream definitions.

  1. def:hecke-normal-form defines H_n(q) as the quotient of the group algebra R[B_n] by the Hecke ideal \langle \sigma_i^2 - (q-q^{-1})\sigma_i - 1 \rangle. The standard T_w basis is then well-defined.
  2. def:categorical-action ensures that the braiding c_{V,V} in \mathbf{C} obeys the Hecke relation (the categorical specialisation that makes \rho_n factor through H_n(q)).

The rewriter's confluence is structural. The Diamond Lemma guarantees that any reduction order reaches the same normal form, since the Hecke and braid relations are linear quadratic and mutually compatible.

Complexity

Worst case: exponential in n (the partition count for H_n(q)). Polynomial in |w| after caching cycle-equivalent words. For nucleon-scale knots (n \leq 9, |w| \leq 24) the reducer finishes in milliseconds on the Rust core.

Python / Rust API entry point

# Per-particle Hecke normal forms (the user-facing surface):
from pyhecke import (
    build_nucleon_nf, build_atom_nf, build_atom_nf_exact,
)

nf_proton  = build_nucleon_nf("proton")
nf_atom    = build_atom_nf(Z=2, N=2)        # ⁴He
nf_exact   = build_atom_nf_exact(Z=2, N=2)  # symbolic

The Rust core is at tools/hecke-engine/src/gb_nf_reducer.rs (canonical implementation, called via the pyhecke-native PyO3 wheel from the builders above).

Witness contract

Canonical witness: hecke-core-symbolic-migration.witness.json. Records the input braid, the output basis-decomposition vector, the chosen q evaluation, and a hash of the rewriter source for reproducibility. Per-particle assemblies are captured in markov-trace-assembly-{proton,neutron,deuteron}.derivation.json (consumed by Step 3).

Notes

The reducer is the single source of Hecke normal forms in the pipeline. Every downstream algorithm consumes NF(w), not the raw braid. Treating the normal form as the canonical object makes the subsequent chain q-rational.
